newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris court keeps asset freeze on ex-Yugoslavia.
newsitem.headline: Paris court keeps asset freeze on ex-Yugoslavia.

text.p: A Paris court on Tuesday maintained a freeze on assets of former Yugoslavia held in French banks despite opposition by Belgrade, a lawyer said.

The court also ordered French banks to disclose any deposits or withdrawals made since the end of 1990 on accounts belonging to former Yugoslavia, said Christian Feddal, a lawyer for Croatia, Macedonia and Bosnia. The three states had pushed for the freeze along with Slovenia.

The four states have sought the freeze until the end of talks dividing up assets between the states of former Yugoslavia, fearing that rump Yugoslavia -- Serbia and Montenegro -- would otherwise have sole control.
The head of the Slovenian Succession Fund, Andrej Rant, estimated last week that there were about $590 million of former Yugoslav assets in nine French banks.

The banks are Societe General, Paribas, Credit Commercial de France, Banque Francaise du Commerce Exterieur, Credit Agricole, Banque Nationale de Paris, Banque Commerciale pour l'Europe du Nord, Credit Lyonnais and Banque Franco-Yugoslave.

"We don't know if there have been any movements in or out of these accounts," Feddal said. After the break-up of Yugoslavia, all assets of the former federation held abroad were frozen in line with a U.N. resolution which expired last November.
